standard_prerequisites.name: The Mittag-Leffler condition and limits
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that a quotient of a Mittag-Leffler system is Mittag-Leffler and that the limit of a short exact sequence of inverse systems is exact when the left term is Mittag-Leffler, which is applied twice.

standard_prerequisites.name: Limits commute with kernels
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the standard identification of the limit of the kernels with the kernel of the limit
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the description of the limit of the kernel systems appearing in the proof.

core_obligations: Setup (proof lines 7930-7936): with the kernel systems of the last map and the image systems of the first map displayed, the limit of the kernel systems is the kernel of the limit map, and the systems form a short exact sequence as displayed.
First application (proof lines 7937-7938): the system of images is a quotient of the Mittag-Leffler system in the first term, hence is Mittag-Leffler.

Second application and conclusion (proof lines 7939-7942): the Mittag-Leffler lemma applied to the displayed short exact sequence shows that the induced map of limits is surjective, which is exactly the exactness of the sequence of limits in the middle.
proof_roadmap: Identify the kernel and image systems and the short exact sequence they form.
Get the Mittag-Leffler property for the images from the hypothesis on the first system.
Apply the Mittag-Leffler limit statement to obtain surjectivity onto the kernel.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that in an exact sequence of inverse systems of abelian groups whose first term satisfies the Mittag-Leffler condition, the induced sequence of limits is exact in the middle (statement lines 7916-7928). The proof is a complete argument: the kernel and image systems are introduced and identified with the kernel of the limit map (proof lines 7930-7936), the image system inherits the Mittag-Leffler property as a quotient of the first system (proof lines 7937-7938), and the limit statement applied to the displayed short exact sequence gives surjectivity onto the kernel of the limit map, which is the claimed exactness (proof lines 7939-7942). The non-formal content is the arrangement of the two short exact sequences. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
